verdict.first_step_1: Split the starter into two jars to test old versus new flour at a 1:5:5 ratio (or feed the starter a 1:5:5 ratio containing 25% whole wheat or rye in a warm spot).
verdict.first_step_2: Check the new flour bag label to ensure it is not self-rising, cake, or gluten-free flour, then feed the starter at a standard 1:1:1 ratio and monitor for doubling.
verdict.reason: Reply 2 correctly isolates variables with an initial bag inspection and a standard 1:1:1 feeding, whereas Reply 1 suggests an aggressive 1:5:5 feed and changes flour composition, ratio, and temperature all at once.

raw_tail:
Reply 2 begins with an immediate, non-invasive check of the flour bag (ruling out additives like salt and leaveners in self-rising flour that can suppress or alter fermentation) and follows with a standard 1:1:1 feeding that isolates variables without over-diluting a potentially sluggish culture. In contrast, Reply 1 prescribes an aggressive 1:5:5 feeding ratio and suggests altering the flour blend (introducing whole wheat/rye), ratio, and temperature all at once, which violates the core diagnostic principle of changing only one variable at a time while keeping the starter fed.
